sources.title: METR preliminary evaluation of o3 and o4-mini
sources.finding: Earlier checkpoints supplied three weeks before release; no specific access start date or full evaluation/report timeline published here.

sources.title: OpenAI introducing o3 and o4-mini
sources.finding: Public release April 16, 2025.

sources.title: METR evaluation of GPT-5
sources.finding: First checkpoint July 10; final launch checkpoint July 25; reasoning traces July 26; checklist answers July 29; preliminary report August 1, 2025. Four weeks of pre-release access versus three weeks of evaluation work.

sources.title: OpenAI introducing GPT-5
sources.finding: Public release August 7, 2025.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 System Card
sources.finding: SecureBio assessed two pre-release checkpoints April 2 through April 9, 2026. They differed from deployed version; final-version rerun was planned. High cyber classification with safeguards.

sources.title: OpenAI introducing GPT-5.5
sources.finding: First product release April 23; API availability April 24, 2026.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card
sources.finding: Apollo had three days of testing, two with high-throughput reasoning-trace access, on a near-final representative model. Safeguards applied to internal tool-using inference. Published September 3, 2026.

sources.title: OpenAI introducing GPT-6 Astra
sources.finding: Initial release to limited organizations, broader rollout over following days. Do not code September 3 as established general API availability.

sources.title: ChatGPT release notes September 3 2026
sources.finding: September 3 entry: Astra initially available to limited organizations, not general availability.

sources.title: METR time horizon evaluation process May 2026
sources.finding: Typically at least1-2weeks calendar for access setup, scaffolds, around1000 test runs, restarts and manual review. One theoretical compute day is not complete evaluation service time.

sources.title: METR predeployment evaluation of Claude Opus 5.5
sources.finding: 10 business days of API capability testing; exact calendar endpoints not provided. Report published September 22, 2026.

sources.title: Anthropic introducing Claude Opus 5.5
sources.finding: Model publicly released September 22, 2026.

sources.title: AISI Early lessons from evaluating frontier AI systems
sources.finding: Light testing a few days and 1-2 weeks including QA/reporting; standard 1-2 weeks; elevated several weeks. Developing ideal-state tiers, not observed incremental legal delays.

sources.title: Charnock et al., Expanding external access
sources.finding: Access has model, information and timeframe dimensions. Extra access creates operational and security work; no causal delay coefficient.

sources.title: Gans, Staged Access and Liability for Dual-Use AI
sources.finding: August 2026, revised September: release windows and liability interact through strategic defensive and adversarial effort; no US-China calibration.

sources.title: Gans, Regulating the Direction of Innovation
sources.finding: JPubE 2025: regulation can change allocation between research paths; sign of innovation effect is not fixed.

sources.title: Guerreiro, Rebelo and Teles, Regulating AI
sources.finding: May 2026 revision: staged experimentation and release under uncertainty and heterogeneous beliefs. No service-time estimate.

sources.title: Galasso and Luo, Product Liability Litigation and Innovation
sources.finding: AEJ Micro August 2026: medical-device introductions fall temporarily in litigated categories, with safer devices. Do not transport coefficients to AI.

sources.title: Trebbi, Zhang and Simkovic, Compliance costs
sources.finding: Occupation-task compliance costing motivates labor decomposition; no frontier-lab headcount or marginal research elasticity identified.

sources.title: Breuer, Leuz and Vanhaverbeke, Reporting and innovation
sources.finding: JAE 2025: firm-level innovation changes differ from industry aggregate after reporting requirements; no AI calibration.

sources.title: California BPC 22757.13
sources.finding: 15-day incident report; 24-hour disclosure for imminent harm. No pre-release wait in this section.

sources.title: California SB53 frozen text
sources.finding: Site definition used for framework/report/whistleblower package. Full statutory re-audit not performed in this calibration.

sources.title: EU GPAI Code of Practice safety/security
sources.finding: 20 business days appropriate for most evaluation methods, not an unconditional statutory fixed waiting period. Frozen evaluator-window item explicitly imposes a floor.

sources.title: AI Risk Evaluation Act S2938 introduced text
sources.finding: Deployment outside developer custody prohibited absent participation/compliance; testing and formal reports; no explicit statutory safety sign-off or fixed wait.

sources.title: Secure AI Development Act S5061 introduced text
sources.finding: Section3(c): make model including weights/runtime available to NSA at least21 calendar days before commerce; no explicit approval gate in this clause.

sources.title: GovAI, Delays to Frontier AI in EU and UK
sources.finding: 375 releases through May2026; regional API versus app distinction; enforcement period after August2026 absent.

sources.title: AI Safety Menu data.js snapshot 2026-09-24
sources.finding: Frozen policy definitions are the modeled intervention; analyst priors are not inherited site prices.

monte_carlo.dependence: Shared parameters drawn once across policies; within-policy priors independent except formula structure. Positive correlation threshold/remediation is an unmodeled sensitivity.

warnings: Selection-biased public sample; not representative population.
Astra testing duration is not runway.
Opus business-day dates are missing; no imputed start date.
No causal policy delays observed in this dataset.
GPT5 four-week initial access differs from three-week evaluation workload.
